title: Modern version first or original with glosses
statement: Whether learners should meet a hard archaic text first in a modern version, beside one, or only in the original with glosses of key words is unsettled.
detail: The sources differ. In a build meeting on 7 October 2026, one participant said they read a scene with students in standard English before looking at the original language, yet praised the build's glosses of key words only as support that does not make the text too easy; another recalled that the earlier plan made the original the primary text, with a translation only as an aid; and the build shown used snippets that translated lines into contemporary English (`g9/sources/meeting-notes/Incept Service CoE Catchup - 2026_10_07 10_30 CEST - Notes by Gemini.md`, lines 434-488). A planning meeting on 1 October floated an optional side-by-side modern translation for learners who struggle (`g9/sources/meeting-notes/ELA - CNU + Academics - 2026_10_01 20_30 IST - Notes by Gemini.md`, line 228).
against: A published classroom guide to cutting the opening scene uses no translation and ends: "Celebrate the fact that students made meaning from this scene without any internet explanation or teacher translation" (`g9/sources/Cutting-a-Scene-Othello-1.1.pdf`, pdftotext lines 140-141).
